name: mini-swe-agent
label: mini-SWE-agent
description: A minimal shell-based coding agent for fixing issues and modifying code in a workspace.

check_ready.not_ready_message: mini-SWE-agent CLI detected. Configure a model through environment variables (MSWEA_MODEL_NAME + a provider key), a full config file (MSWEA_MINI_CONFIG_PATH), or the Model field before running a task.

env_config.name: MSWEA_MODEL_NAME
env_config.description: Model to use (routed through LiteLLM), e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 or gpt-4o. Optional when a model is already configured via a config file or `mini-extra config setup`. Passed as --model.

env_config.name: MSWEA_MINI_CONFIG_PATH
env_config.description: Path to a FULL mini config file (YAML). Optional. This REPLACES mini's built-in default config (agent prompt templates, step/environment settings) — it does not merge — so provide a complete file (a good starting point is the output of `mini-extra config setup`). Leave blank to use mini's default config.

env_config.name: MSWEA_COST_LIMIT
env_config.description: Optional per-run cost limit in USD, passed as --cost-limit. Leave blank for mini's default.

env_config.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env_config.description: Anthropic API key — used when the model is an Anthropic model. Leave blank if using another provider or a key already in your environment.

env_config.name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
env_config.description: Custom endpoint for native `anthropic/…` models (an enterprise gateway or Anthropic-protocol relay). Leave blank for hosted Anthropic. Note: most third-party relays are OpenAI-compatible — for those use an `openai/…` model + OPENAI_BASE_URL instead.

env_config.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
env_config.description: OpenAI API key — used when the model is an OpenAI model. Leave blank if using another provider or a key already in your environment.

env_config.name: OPENAI_BASE_URL
env_config.description: Custom endpoint for OpenAI-compatible models (a relay/proxy or self-hosted gateway) — applies only to `openai/…` models. Leave blank for hosted OpenAI, or for native providers like `deepseek/…` / `anthropic/…`.

env_config.name: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
env_config.description: DeepSeek API key — used when the model is a `deepseek/…` model (e.g. deepseek/deepseek-chat or deepseek/deepseek-reasoner). Connects directly to api.deepseek.com; no base URL needed.

env_config.name: DEEPSEEK_API_BASE
env_config.description: Custom endpoint for native `deepseek/…` models. Leave blank to use DeepSeek's default (api.deepseek.com).

tagline: A minimal shell-based SWE agent, ~100 lines of Python.

name: openworker
label: OpenWorker
description: Local-first agent coworker driven headlessly through its own server

check_ready.not_ready_message: No model API key — pick a provider and set OPENWORKER_API_KEY (press e to configure)
check_ready.unreadable_message: The OpenWorker model key could not be read. Re-enter OPENWORKER_API_KEY in the Configure screen.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_PROVIDER
env_config.description: Which model provider the API key belongs to. OpenWorker is bring-your-own-model, so this decides both the endpoint and how the model id is routed. Use ollama for a local server, or openai-codex to reuse a ChatGPT subscription (which also needs OPENWORKER_STATE_DIR).

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_API_KEY
env_config.description: API key for the provider selected above. Passed to the OpenWorker server in its environment and never written to disk. Leave blank only for ollama, or when reusing a state directory that already holds credentials.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_BASE_URL
env_config.description: Endpoint override — for a relay, a self-hosted gateway, Azure OpenAI, or where `ollama serve` is listening. Leave blank to use the provider's official endpoint.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_MODEL
env_config.description: Model id to run on. Leave empty for the OpenWorker default; the provider prefix is added automatically, so plain `claude-opus-5` is enough when the provider is anthropic.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_MODE
env_config.description: Permission mode for each turn. `bypass-approvals` is the default because nobody is at the keyboard to approve tool calls; its hard floors (settings files, writes outside the workspace, .git/hooks) still apply. `interactive` and `auto-approve` will stall on anything that asks.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_ALLOW_TOOL_INSTALL
env_config.description: Set to 1 to let the agent install tools from OpenWorker's pinned catalog on its own. Off by default — a declined request is a supported outcome and the agent falls back and says so.

env_config.name: OPENWORKER_STATE_DIR
env_config.description: Advanced. Where the OpenWorker server keeps its conversations and credentials. Blank means a private directory under ~/.openagents. Point it at the desktop app's state directory (~/.config/coworker, or %APPDATA%\coworker) to reuse its sign-ins — but only while that app is closed, since two processes must never write one store.

tagline: Everything stays on your machine: the agent loop, the conversations, the model keys. Installed with uv.

name: codebuddy
label: CodeBuddy Code (WorkBuddy)
description: Tencent's CodeBuddy Code CLI — the same engine the WorkBuddy desktop app runs, driven headlessly
tagline: The terminal agent behind Tencent's WorkBuddy desktop app — same engine, same account, driven headlessly. Installed with npm.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_REGION
env_config.description: Which CodeBuddy site the account belongs to. `international` is codebuddy.ai / workbuddy.ai (Google or GitHub sign-in); `china` is codebuddy.cn / workbuddy.cn. An account only exists on one of them, and picking the wrong one fails as a login error rather than a routing error.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_API_KEY
env_config.description: CodeBuddy API key, for running without an interactive sign-in. Optional — leave blank if you signed in by running `codebuddy` and using /login on this machine.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN
env_config.description: Platform auth token, the alternative to an API key (an enterprise PAT, for example). Paste the token itself; a leading `Bearer ` is stripped for you.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_MODEL
env_config.description: Model id to run on. Leave empty for the account default. The CLI also accepts its aliases — default-model, fast-model, deep-model — which keep working when the underlying model is replaced.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_EFFORT
env_config.description: Reasoning effort for each run. Leave empty for the model's own default.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_MAX_TURNS
env_config.description: Maximum agentic turns per message. Leave empty for the CLI default; a run that hits the limit still returns the answer it reached.

env_config.name: CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL
env_config.description: Advanced. Endpoint override, for an enterprise or self-hosted deployment. Blank means the endpoint the region above selects.

check_ready.not_ready_message: Not signed in for this site. Sign in with the Login button — it opens the CLI on the site CODEBUDDY_REGION selects, where you run /login — or set CODEBUDDY_API_KEY / CODEBUDDY_AUTH_TOKEN (press e). A session for the other site does not carry over: the CLI keeps only one, and codebuddy.ai and codebuddy.cn are separate accounts.
